name: North Face
text: [overview] The first ascent stayed mostly on the rock walls, crossing between them to avoid snow and ice.
[overview] After heavy winters snow persists in the couloir into fall and turns to blue alpine ice at about 50 degrees.
[overview] If returning to Second Recess, take the Northwest ridge, also called the Glacier Route (class 2).
[detailed_rack] Bring screws and pickets for ice, plus some rock gear, chosen to suit conditions and your comfort.
earlierWhy: why: Couloir holds snow into fall and turns to ice; the glacier on the peak is not settled.

name: North Face
text: [overview] The climb crosses the glacier to a clear couloir centered on the north face, ascends it (about 40 degrees) until a solid rock cap stops it, then veers right onto gentler terrain, mostly 3rd class, to reach the flat top before the summit itself.
[detailed_rack] Always: helmet, crampons and axe(s).
[approach] Descend a broad, low-angle scree chute, turn south and go up the recess, passing Snow Lakes, to reach the glacier under the north face.
earlierWhy: why: The text says the party crosses a glacier below the face, but it is a small Sierra glacier and its hazard is unclear.

name: Hotlum-Wintun Ridge
text: [overview] from there climb straight up between the two glaciers, Hotlum and Wintun.
[overview] Above 11,000' it steepens and two snowfields, each close to 45 degrees, flank a rocky tongue.
[overview] Most parties traverse climber's left onto the Wintun Glacier above;
[detailed_rack] Snow climbing gear at a basic level, and skis or a snowboard are strongly advised.
[approach] The trail is faint and disappears under snow, so head up toward the summit, which stays in view, along the open slopes south of the Brewer Creek drainage.
[approach] The route climbs the broad snowfield above the camp between the Hotlum and Wintun glaciers, so recognise the start by the large snowfield rising straight above the bench.

[descent_text] From the summit, angle down the steep upper chute and onto the Wintun side, where the slope is steepest and a fall can slide a long way, so keep the axe in hand and do not glissade carelessly.
[descent_text] Cross back over the rib to the snowfield between the glaciers, below the high traverse, then run down the snowfield to the bench camp and the Brewer Creek drainage to the trailhead.
[descent_text] The route has no major crevasses or fumaroles, but the snow can turn to heavy slush in the afternoon.
earlierWhy: why: Climbs between two glaciers and traverses onto the Wintun Glacier, though the text says no major crevasses.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Climbs a 700-ft snow and ice couloir, about 40 degrees, to the gap between this peak and Mount Williams.
earlierWhy: why: A snow and ice couloir on a peak that has a glacier at its base, and the text does not place the line on it. | secondReview: no/yes: The route is a snow and ice couloir with no glacier named on the line.

name: North Arete
text: [overview] many options exist, but joining it higher up means firm snow late in the season.
earlierWhy: why: Rock arete, but the text mentions firm late-season snow without saying where the approach goes. | secondReview: unsure/yes: Banner Peak carries glacier ice nearby and the text does not place the arete clear of it; snow is firm late.

name: North Couloir
text: [overview] The bergschrund, at 11,700', is crossed first, then about 1200' of couloir averaging 40 degrees, steepening slightly near the top, leads to the col.
[detailed_rack] Take a modest set of rock gear and maybe one or two pickets, as comfort dictates.
earlierWhy: why: A couloir above a bergschrund at 11,700 ft, so a permanent snow or ice body is likely but not described.

name: South Face
text: [detailed_rack] Small alpine rack of the usual kind, plus an ice axe in season.
earlierWhy: why: Ice axe only in season; peak not verified. | secondReview: no/unsure: Ice axe is only listed in season; no snow on the line is described.

name: Northeast Couloir
text: [overview] The bergschrund can be large, and pitch 1 beyond it is an ice smear, vertical in places, over a bulge.
[overview] A snowfield above ranges from deep facets to hard neve.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons
earlierWhy: why: Bergschrund and snowfield above ice; glacier crevasse hazard not settled.

name: Piper at the Gates of Dawn
text: [overview] Cracks plus a pair of roofs gain the slab's top, then easy ground by a snowfield and a traverse to a small arete bring you onto the summit ridge.
earlierWhy: why: Passes a snowfield near the Palisade area; glacier contact not settled.

name: Twilight Pillar
text: [overview] Gain the ridge right below where Firebird Ridge begins, traverse left beneath the major snowfield onto the lower part of the pillar, and follow the lower 5th class ridge to a ledge under the upper headwall.
[what_to_bring] ice axe — early in the season, for ice
earlierWhy: why: Traverses beneath a major snowfield; glacier and normal-day snow not settled. | secondReview: no/no: The axe is only for early-season ice. | research: unsure/yes: A trip report says the standard approach crosses the glacier or skirts a permanent snowfield below the pillar, and other notes call for an axe early in the season.

name: Queen's Way
text: [overview] A route up Apache by way of the Isabelle Glacier, entering from the head of the South Saint Vrain valley.

[approach] From the Brainard Lake area start at the Long Lake trailhead and follow the Pawnee Pass trail past Long Lake to Lake Isabelle, then continue west along the Isabelle Glacier trail to the tarn below Navajo, Apache and Shoshoni peaks.
[approach] Cross the Isabelle Glacier to its southwest corner, where the route climbs a steep snow ramp to a saddle below the summit.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
earlierWhy: why: Crosses the Isabelle Glacier then a steep snow ramp; crevasse hazard there is not settled.

name: Six Pack of Beer & Nothing to Do
text: [overview] Mostly consistent ice with a few snow slopes.
[approach] The face holds snow-catching basins, so check the avalanche forecast.
earlierWhy: why: Winter ice with snow slopes and avalanche basins; could not confirm the face has no glacier.

name: Canmore Wedding Party
text: [approach] In winter the road to the Granite Lake trailhead near Libby is unplowed past the end of the pavement, so the trip starts on skis or foot or by snowmobile and is long, then the trail follows Granite Creek to the lake.
[approach] The couloirs funnel snow, so check the avalanche forecast.
earlierWhy: why: Winter ice and mixed couloir route in the Cabinets, where no glacier is travelled; snow is the season. | secondReview: unsure/yes: The face lies below the remnant Blackwell Glacier and no source rules out glacier contact.

name: The Bull River Prowler
text: [overview] A moderate route for stable snow, perhaps comparable in scale to Dragon Tail Peak's Triple Couloirs.
[overview] Traverse left on a snowy ledge, up a rightward runnel to the lower snowfield, then up-left to a couloir zigzagging right to the band of rock higher up.
[overview] a chimney choked with snow may be the crux.
[overview] Dig through the cornice to the summit ridge.
